rows.description: The person writes the hurt in a private note, talks to a trusted friend and channels the energy into exercise or study. Letting the anger be felt safely stops it from turning into action that adds new harm.
graph_context: next stage: Facing the loss
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: anger, trust, hurt

rows.subtype: Stage 5: Deciding to release the grudge [Response]
rows.description: The person chooses to stop carrying the resentment for their own peace, perhaps by writing an unsent letter or talking it through. Forgiveness is a choice for oneself and does not require the other's apology.
graph_context: next stage: Boundaries and reconciliation choices
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: calm, resentment

rows.description: Forgiving does not mean returning to the same trust. The person decides whether to renew contact, keep distance or rebuild slowly, depending on remorse and safety, and is never obliged to stay near someone who harms them.
graph_context: previous stage: Deciding to release the grudge
next stage: Self-forgiveness
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: guilt, trust

rows.description: Where the person themself caused harm, they own it, make amends where possible and allow themselves to grow rather than punishing forever. Guilt that leads to repair is healthy, while endless shame helps no one.
graph_context: previous stage: Boundaries and reconciliation choices
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: shame, guilt

rows.description: At a reunion or on social media, a 25-year-old sees peers with more money, a spouse, a startup or an abroad degree. The gap suddenly makes their own path look small and late.
graph_context: next stage: Counting the roads not taken
related mind states: surprise

rows.subtype: Stage 2: Counting the roads not taken [Actor]
rows.description: The person lists lost chances such as the course they skipped, the person they let go or the year they wasted. Regret sharpens when choices were shaped by family pressure or fear, not desire.
graph_context: previous stage: Comparison shock
next stage: Fear of being behind
related mind states: fear, regret

rows.description: The person feels time is running out, with pressure to marry, earn and settle by a supposed deadline. Social clocks, especially in tight-knit communities, make normal variation feel like failure.
graph_context: previous stage: Counting the roads not taken
next stage: Restless drastic thoughts
related mind states: fear

rows.description: Thoughts arise of quitting the job, leaving the city or ending a relationship overnight. The urge for change is often a signal about unmet needs, but impulsive moves do not always meet them.
graph_context: previous stage: Fear of being behind
next stage: Sorting regret from values
related mind states: boredom

rows.description: A parent or friend hears a restless declaration and either panics or dismisses it. Asking what is missing and helping test small changes treats the feeling as information, not as a crisis.
graph_context: previous stage: Fear of being behind
next stage: Sorting regret from values
related mind states: boredom

rows.description: The person separates regrets about actions they can still fix from things beyond change, and asks what they truly value rather than what they are supposed to want. This turns vague dread into a direction.
graph_context: previous stage: Restless drastic thoughts
next stage: Small experiments
related mind states: fear, regret
